narrative_markdown:
## Company overview

NVIDIA Corporation (NVDA) is a Technology-sector company in the Semiconductors industry, with a market capitalization of $5.65T. It describes itself as a data center scale AI infrastructure company, selling in the United States, Taiwan, China, Hong Kong, Europe and internationally. It reports through two segments: Compute & Networking, and Graphics.

Compute & Networking covers data center accelerated computing and networking platforms, AI solutions and software, and automotive platforms including autonomous and electric vehicle solutions. Graphics offers GeForce GPUs for gaming and PCs, and Quadro/NVIDIA RTX GPUs for enterprise workstation graphics. The shares trade at $233.95, within a 52-week range of 164.27-237.87.

## Financial commentary

Revenue has grown in each year shown, from $26.97B in fiscal 2023 to $60.92B in fiscal 2024, $130.50B in fiscal 2025 and $215.94B in fiscal 2026. Net income rose even faster, from $4.37B to $29.76B, then $72.88B, and $120.07B in fiscal 2026.

Profitability is very high. Net margin is 63.7% and return on equity is 117.2%. Revenue growth is reported at 105.9%. Leverage is modest, with debt/equity of 0.17, and the dividend yield is 0.4%. A recent news item notes an increase of $150 Billion to the share repurchase authorization.

## Comps commentary

The comparison uses forward P/E as the primary multiple. NVIDIA's forward P/E of 14.9 sits 63% below the peer median of 40.3. Its trailing P/E of 29.2 is 56% below the peer median of 66.8. On enterprise-value measures the discount is smaller: EV/EBITDA of 27.9 is 26% below the median of 37.9, and EV/Revenue of 18.5 is 5% below the median of 19.4.

The fundamentals differ sharply from the peer group. Net margin of 63.7% is 203% above the peer median of 21.0%, and revenue growth of 105.9% is 190% above the median of 36.5%. Debt/equity of 0.17 is 65% below the median of 0.49. The peers are AMD, Broadcom, Intel, Marvell and Qualcomm, and their results vary widely, which makes the median a rough yardstick.

## Risk commentary

Three risks are rated most severe. First, shifting and expanding US export controls over three years have affected the company's ability to serve customers outside the United States. Second, competitors could take market share and hurt financial results. Third, long manufacturing lead times, uncertain supply and capacity, and inaccurate demand forecasts have caused and could cause supply and demand mismatches.

Three further risks are rated a notch lower. Reliance on third-party manufacturers to make, assemble, test and package products reduces control over quantity, quality, yields and delivery schedules. Failing to meet the changing needs of its industry and markets could hurt results. Product defects have caused and could cause significant remediation expenses and damage the business. The recent news headlines do not bear directly on these risks.
